subject: Bridgewater - on-prem residency / network constraints (recap + asks)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bridgewaterhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Bridgewater - on-prem residency / network constraints (recap + asks)

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick written recap so we have a shared checklist and clear next steps. I copied Ben (sales engineering) and Naomi (account lead) to coordinate the technical follow-ups and commercial path.

Call summary (short):
- Business driver: Bring Redwood inference into a strictly isolated on-prem enclave to support PHI workloads for a planned pilot in Q4. Primary goals are low-latency inference for clinician workflows and strict data residency controls.
- Regulatory drivers: HIPAA + internal SOC program; Bridgewater requires audit-able access logs and customer-managed key controls where possible.
- Networking constraints discussed:
  * No direct egress from enclave to public internet.
  * All outbound traffic must go through a proxied jump host / industrial NAT managed by Bridgewater ops.
  * Control-plane connectivity: customer prefers private peering (Direct Connect / ExpressRoute) rather than hosted-control-plane internet callbacks.

Open pain points we agreed to validate:
1) Exact network egress pattern for model downloads and runtime callbacks (can Bridgewater host a model-artifact mirror in-artifact-repo behind NAT?).
2) KMS requirements — customer-managed KMS or HSM mandatory for keys that encrypt persisted PHI-derived artifacts.
3) RBAC / audit log requirements — specifics on retention period and log export format for our telemetry.

Proposed next steps (action owners):
- Ben: provide a short schematic of how Redwood runtime can run in an air-gapped enclave (attached) and a checklist of required firewall rules / ports. (Ben will add notes on model sync options).
- Naomi: lead commercial checklist & procurement intro; please confirm the procurement timeline and any required security questionnaires.
- Alex / Bridgewater: share network diagram and any compliance acceptance criteria (SOC2 scope, required attestations).

Attachments: redwood-private-architecture.pdf (high-level runtime layout; includes model-sync options).

Timebox: we'd like to lock technical feasibility by 2028-09-12 so we can scope a two-week pilot. Can you confirm availability for a technical follow-up with your network engineer and CISO next week?

Thanks again — Stephanie

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bridgewaterhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@bridgewaterhealth.com, Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@bridgewaterhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 09:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Bridgewater - on-prem residency / network constraints (recap + asks)

Stephanie — really helpful recap, appreciate the clear asks. A few clarifications from our side and I attached our internal network sketch (bridgewater-network-diagram-v1.pdf) for reference.

Clarifications / constraints:
- Enclave policy: all compute nodes have zero egress to public internet by default. We can provide a managed NAT/proxy jump host that your runtime can use for outbound artifact pulls, but it has to be authenticated and rate-limited.
- Model artifacts: we can host an artifact mirror in our internal repo (Artifactory) accessible via the jump host. We will need an integration plan for initial model syncs and periodic updates.
- Control plane: we cannot accept persistent outbound callbacks to a public control plane. If Redwood requires any control-plane connectivity, that traffic must be over a private peering (we prefer ExpressRoute).
- KMS: we operate a customer-managed KMS (Cloud HSM) and expect vendors to either support customer-side key management or provide FIPS/HSM-wrapped keys.

Next steps from us:
- I'll loop in our network architect (cc'd procurement and Maria).
- Maria (CISO) will list specific audit/retention requirements; she suggested a short security working session next Tue 11 Sep (10:00–11:00 ET).
- Procurement: I'll share expected contracting terms and any vendor security questionnaire items.

We're interested in a proof-of-concept but need the above conditions satisfied. Happy to run a 60m technical+security session next Tue if that works for your team.

— Alex
Alex Turner
Director of Platform Engineering, Bridgewater Health
alex.turner@bridgewaterhealth.com | (617) 555-0199

Attachment: bridgewater-network-diagram-v1.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bridgewaterhealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridgewater - on-prem residency / network constraints (recap + asks)

Alex / team — thanks. Quick technical notes and what I'll bring to the next session: 

1) Architecture options we validated internally (high-level):
  - Air-gapped mode: runtime and model store co-located inside your enclave; model sync via authenticated jump host and signed artifacts. No outbound runtime callbacks required.
  - Peered control-plane: private ExpressRoute peering for telemetry and control-plane ops (fallback: offline operation with batch-sidecar uploads to S3 behind your peering).

2) Ports & firewall: minimum outbound allowed (via proxy) — TCP 443 for artifact fetches, optional TCP 22 for secure model push (SSH sync) if you prefer pull vs push. We'll prepare a one-page firewall whitelist.

3) KMS / keys: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS; we can wire to your Cloud HSM. We also offer envelope encryption so persisted model caches and any derived embeddings can be encrypted with your keys. Need to confirm HSM algorithm support and key rotation cadence.

Action items (from Redwood):
- I'll produce a simple firewall whitelist + artifact sync pattern doc (by EOD Thu 2028-09-07).
- Stephanie / Naomi — I'll coordinate a 60m security + network call next Tue and bring an architect.
- We'll also prepare a one-page pilot SOW draft covering timebox, success criteria, and a 2-week pilot runbook.

Link to working folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-Bridgewater-MAP (I'll add the whitelist there).

Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0108
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@bridgewaterhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@bridgewaterhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@bridgewaterhealth.com, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Sep 2028 09:11:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Bridgewater - on-prem residency / network constraints (recap + asks)

Team — adding the CISO lens. A few mandatory items from Bridgewater security before we can move to pilot: 

- KMS/HSM: any keys that encrypt PHI must be under our customer-managed HSM. We require key-wrapping proofs and an explanation of your envelope encryption approach.
- Audit logs: vendor must provide immutable audit logs for access to models and inference requests (we need detail on what fields you capture, retention, and export format). Minimum retention we require is 7 years for PHI-related events.
- Data residency: all persisted artifacts and backups for PHI workloads must be stored in our us-east-1 tenancy.
- Pen test / intake: we require a current pentest summary and any open high/critical findings to be disclosed ahead of pilot.

Please prepare:
1) Short one-page KMS integration note (how Redwood integrates with customer HSMs).
2) Audit-log schema and retention plan.
3) Current SOC2 report or attestation and pentest summary.

We are available for the security working session on Tue 2028-09-11 10:00–11:00 ET (Alex, please confirm). If Redwood can produce the three items above prior to that call, we can discuss a timeboxed pilot scope.

Regards,
Maria Gomez
Chief Information Security Officer
Bridgewater Health
